sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus landed location (Malapert A region)
Mons Mouton feature centre (representative marker for announced VIPER region)

sources.productId: Apollo Landing Site Coordinates; Apollo 11/12/14/15/16/17 Lunar Module rows
sources.agency: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, National Space Science Data Center (NSSDCA)
sources.coordinateFrame: Planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis Lunar Reference System, DE421 ephemeris (as stated by source).
sources.usageTerms: No explicit license stated on source page. Factual coordinates transcribed with attribution; check NASA terms before redistributing source text or imagery.
sources.evidence: The page explicitly identifies the frame and gives each Lunar Module latitude and east longitude. Values retained at the precision published by NASA.
sources.coordinatePrecision: As published: 5 decimal places for Apollo 11/14/15; 4 for Apollo 12/16/17.

sources.productId: NASA LRO images IM-1 Odysseus; LROC NAC frame M1463440322L
sources.agency: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Arizona State University
sources.coordinateFrame: Not specified by this source; use only its rounded published coordinates, without asserting a named realization.
sources.usageTerms: NASA content; NASA/Goddard/ASU attribution shown, no explicit license statement. Check NASA/ASU terms before reusing text or imagery.
sources.evidence: Source says landed at 80.13° south, 1.44° east and elevation 8,461 ft (2,579 m); frame M1463440322L. Coordinates are rounded to 0.01°.
sources.coordinatePrecision: 0.01° as published; no more precision inferred.

sources.productId: LROC featured image “Blue Ghost Lunar Lander Seen From Above”; NAC M1495619099LR
sources.agency: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University LROC Science Operations Center
sources.coordinateFrame: Not specified by this source; no ME/PA or DE421 precision is asserted.
sources.usageTerms: Follow https://www.lroc.im-ldi.com/about/terms; credit NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University.
sources.evidence: Source explicitly reports landed Blue Ghost coordinates 18.5623°N, 61.8103°E, elevation -3650 m, at image center.
sources.coordinatePrecision: 0.0001° as published; no more precision inferred.

sources.productId: NASA release: NASA Selects Mons Mouton for VIPER Moon Rover Touchdown
sources.coordinateFrame: No point coordinates/frame published; historical selection of named Mons Mouton region only.
sources.usageTerms: NASA release; no explicit license stated. Attribute NASA and check NASA terms before reuse.
sources.evidence: At announcement time NASA selected Mons Mouton as a VIPER planned touchdown region, but supplied no point coordinate. The Site point is separately sourced as USGS Gazetteer feature centre, not touchdown point.
sources.coordinatePrecision: No point coordinates published by NASA; no point precision claimed.

sources.productId: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature feature 16070 Mons Mouton; Control Network LOLA 2011
sources.agency: USGS Astrogeology Science Center / IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature (NASA-supported)
sources.coordinateFrame: Planetographic, east-positive, longitude [-180, 180], as stated in the Gazetteer; centre of named feature.
sources.usageTerms: USGS/DOI website; follow applicable USGS legal/site terms and attribute Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature / IAU.
sources.evidence: Feature record explicitly gives Mons Mouton centre at -84.60°, +31.00° and approximate diameter 130 km. Used only as representative point for the named planned region, never as touchdown point.
sources.coordinatePrecision: 0.01° as published for the feature centre; no touchdown precision claimed.
